card.occupation: Self-employed wall and floor tiler, part-time, roughly 10 to 14 hours a week. He mostly does bathroom splashbacks, kitchen floors and small repair jobs that come through his dad's friends, neighbours and a builder mate in Harlow. Some of the work is cash in hand.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive. He started A-levels in PE and business at sixth form and dropped out partway through Year 12. Later he did an NVQ Level 2 in Wall and Floor Tiling at Harlow College in his early twenties, after a couple of years in warehouse and bar jobs.
card.household: Lives back in his childhood home, a four-bed 1980s detached house on an estate on the edge of town. His parents are married and still live there: his dad Graham is a recently semi-retired chartered surveyor, and his mum Karen is a practice manager at a GP surgery. Lewis moved back in at 31 after splitting up with his long-term girlfriend, when he couldn't cover the rent on their flat on his own. His older sister is married and lives in Cambridge.
card.cultural_background: White British, born at the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow and raised in Bishop's Stortford. He has a comfortable middle-class upbringing, though he leans more towards his mates' laddish, practical world than his parents' professional one. He was christened and confirmed Church of England and ticks 'Christian' on forms. In practice he only goes to church at Christmas and for weddings and funerals, usually because his mum asks.
card.professional_persona: Competent with a tile cutter and good at making a finished job look tidy, but unreliable with scheduling. He turns up late, sometimes lets a quote slide for a week, and prefers jobs where he knows the client will be out. He prices according to how well-off the client looks. He talks a good game about 'building the business up' but turns down work if it clashes with football or a lie-in. He relies on his dad's network rather than advertising.
card.sports_persona: A Tottenham Hotspur fan, like his dad. He watches most games at the Nag's Head or on the sofa at home and goes to a home game a couple of times a season when someone has a spare ticket. He plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights at the leisure centre, more for the pint afterwards than the fitness. He goes golfing occasionally with his dad and gets annoyed at himself when he plays badly.
card.arts_persona: Not interested in galleries, theatre or reading for pleasure. He watches whatever is on Netflix or Sky, mainly crime dramas, Gladiator-type films and football documentaries. He listens to Capital or a Spotify playlist in the van, mostly old garage and whatever is in the charts. He went to a few big festivals in his twenties for the drinking rather than the music.
card.travel_persona: Prefers package holidays somewhere hot with a pool bar. He did lads' holidays to Magaluf, Ayia Napa and Zante in his twenties and stag dos in Prague and Benidorm, and was in Marbella last summer with three mates. He likes Stansted being twenty minutes away. He has no desire to go anywhere 'where you'd have to sort out trains and that'.
card.culinary_persona: Eats what his mum cooks most evenings and calls it dinner. He loves a Sunday roast. When out he goes for Nando's, a mixed grill, a curry after the pub or a McDonald's breakfast between jobs. He can do pasta and a fry-up and not much else. He drinks lager and the odd vodka Red Bull when it's a big night.
hobbies_and_interests: EA Sports FC on the PlayStation, often online with mates
looking at cars online, especially second-hand BMWs and Audis he can't really afford
nights out in Bishop's Stortford and occasionally Chelmsford
the gym, in phases that last a few weeks
skills: wall and floor tiling, including grouting and sealing
chatting to clients and making them feel they're getting a good deal
driving a van and loading it efficiently
decent at five-a-side, plays up front
knows his way around Facebook Marketplace for buying and flipping tools
card.career_goals: Says he'd like to have his own bathroom-fitting company 'with a couple of lads under me' and his name on the van. Realistically he wants enough steady cash work to move out and get a nicer car, without having to work full weeks. He hasn't done anything concrete towards it.
card.voice: Casual southern English with a mild Hertfordshire/Essex edge: dropped t's, 'innit' never but 'yeah' and 'you know' as tags a lot. He uses 'mate' to people he's just met. He says 'sort of' and 'kind of' interchangeably, says 'erm' when caught off guard, and now and then says 'you was'. His pace is easy and a bit lazy, and his answers are short unless the topic is football or money. If there's a silence he fills it with a short laugh and 'yeah, so, dunno really' rather than elaborating. He picks up the interviewer's words and hands them back: 'Satisfied with work? Yeah, I'm sort of satisfied, yeah.'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase with no capital at the start. Few full stops, and commas only occasionally. He skips apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). He uses 'tbh', 'idk' and 'n/a' freely. Answers are a few words, typed fast, with the odd uncorrected typo. For example: 'tiling mostly, do bathrooms n that, part time tbh'.
card.with_strangers: Friendly enough on the surface and easy to talk to. He's a bit cocky and likes to present himself as doing better than he is, for example calling his work 'my business' and implying he's busier than he is. He's not rude, but he doesn't put himself out. He'll rush the boring bits of a survey and perk up if asked his opinion on something he cares about.
small_things: the M11 being a nightmare in the mornings
the price of tile adhesive going up
a car he saw on AutoTrader
a Marbella trip with the lads
Stansted flights being cheap if you book early
deeper_things: he's embarrassed about living back with his parents at 34 and tells people it's 'just while I save up'
the break-up with his ex, Jess, who said he never got his act together
a sense that his dad is quietly disappointed he didn't go to uni like his sister
he owes his parents a couple of grand from when he moved back and hasn't paid much of it
worry that his knees and back won't last if he ever does tiling full-time
a bit of jealousy watching mates buy houses and have kids
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on his lap, angled slightly upward so the ceiling and the top of a door frame are visible. Light comes from a ceiling light and a window off to the left, so one side of his face is brighter. He is a white man in his mid-thirties with a slightly round face, light stubble and short brown hair faded at the sides, a bit longer on top and pushed forward. He has a half-smile, looking just off the screen. No glasses. He wears a navy Nike quarter-zip top. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed Spurs shirt and, lower down, the edge of a single wardrobe with a hoodie hanging on its door. A shelf holds a PlayStation controller, a deodorant can and a couple of small trophies from youth football.
